text: Blocked at continue: aof work next 59 answered blocked on 58 while 58 was accepted and committed on disk (d46a173d). Root cause: 58, 58/00, 58/01 and 58/03 had their status: frontmatter hand-edited to done instead of moving through aof work status, so no item-status.changed event fired and publish-on-mutate never ran. The last full snapshot was 2026-08-29T09:00:34.971Z (every work_items row for the workspace carries that identical updated_at), and the control daemon — whose periodic tick would have self-healed the hand-edit — was not running. buildStreamView overlays the cached status over disk and nextWorkCacheFirst treats the cache as authoritative for the depends gate, so a driver done only on DISK stays blocking its dependents. Repaired by firing a disk-derived publish tick.

Mesh defect, measured twice in one session: a dispatch worktree's publish silently overwrites the control's newer item rows. buildStreamView guards READS from a worktree (isMeshWorktree short-circuits the cache so a worktree answers from its own disk), but the PUBLISH path carries no equivalent guard — publishItemProjection hands publishGlobalWorkSnapshot the worktree as the workspace, and it writes the WHOLE workspace snapshot from that worktree's older disk. Sequence observed: 59/00 set in-review on the control; 59/01 dispatched, its worktree branched from a HEAD predating that write, so it held 59/00 at in-progress; aof work status 59/01 in-progress inside that worktree published the worktree's view and reverted the control's 59/00 row to in-progress. Same failure class as the 58 block that opened this session — the cache disagrees with the authoritative record and nextWorkCacheFirst believes the cache — but reached by a different door, and this one needs no hand edit at all. A publish from a materialised worktree should either be refused or narrowed to the refs the event names, exactly as the operator-authorship rule already narrows publish-on-mutate.

59/04 shipped --strict as TWO divergences from doctor, not one: the audit gates only under --strict AND --strict promotes nothing (a warn-only run exits 0 under it). Only the first half was flagged at build. 15/ADR-002 had explicitly considered and REJECTED that exact policy for doctor, so the divergence read as a drift rather than a decision. Landed as 59/ADR-002 2a + FF-5911 at the milestone close. Retro: when a story reuses a sibling command's contract 'wholesale', the reuse claim needs a cell-by-cell table at build time, not a sentence in STORY Notes (which said 'reused unchanged' and is now false).

A source-text sweep classified a gate's population by the PATH a suite spells, and loadLoops appends the 'loops' segment itself — so two suites reading the whole shipped registry are outside 58/FF-5809's population, and one lane-3 file is inside it only because an assertion MESSAGE contains the string 'src/bundle/loops/'. Same species as the substring registration lane 59 retired (ADR-003 2), one gate over. Ledgered as TECH_DEBT 75. Retro: 59/ADR-003 2's ruling ('registration is decided by runtime membership, never by the runner's source text') should be applied as a sweep over ALL text-classifying gates, not just the one it was written for.
